notes: EDITING A SAVED DRAFT WORKS AGAIN — PLEASE INSTALL THIS IF YOU ARE ON 0.6.64 OR 0.6.65. On those two versions, saving a payment or a receipt as a draft and then re-opening it to change something failed outright, with a message about a voucher being "reclassified between hand-keyed and system-generated". There was no way round it except deleting the draft and keying the whole thing again. Journal entries were not affected, which is why it went unnoticed for two releases. Nothing was ever recorded wrongly — the edit simply refused — but saving a draft and coming back to correct it is one of the most ordinary things anyone does in a day, and it should not have shipped broken. WHY IT HAPPENED, PLAINLY. Version 0.6.64 added a control for a real problem: a draft the system had prepared could be opened, have its lines replaced with a payment to anyone for any amount, and posted with no second signature, because it still carried the system's own mark. That control now marks such a voucher as hand-written the moment a person edits it, so it answers to dual control from then on. The control is right and stays. What was wrong was the direction of an older rule that froze that mark in BOTH directions — so the new mark could never be applied, and the edit was refused instead. The rule now stops only what it was written to stop: a hand-written voucher can never be quietly relabelled as system-made to escape a second signature. A draft can be taken over by a person, which is the point. HOW IT WAS FOUND. Not by a test — by using the finished release the way you would: saving a draft, changing a tax rate, and re-opening the draft to re-price it. No automated check covered that sequence, so one has been added that fails against the broken version. There are no data changes in this release. Back up before installing, as always, then install over the top; your books are untouched.
